```{r gallery-setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7,
  fig.height = 4.8, dpi = 144, out.width = "100%")
options(width = 82)
```

`postrank` provides seven `ggplot2` plotting functions for common-grade
analyses. Every plotting function reads stored `postrank` objects and returns a
`ggplot` object without running an optimization solver, fitting models, or
computing new comparison probabilities (for multidomain grade profiles with a
separate grade in each domain, see `postrank_plot_mdomain()` in
[Grading entities across multiple domains](mdomain-quickstart.html)).

Below we load the stored six-site tutorial objects (`pr_tutorial`, where
independent normal scores have standard deviation `0.2`, larger values mean
higher priority, Grade 1 is highest priority, and sharing a grade leaves a pair
unordered without claiming equal scores) alongside the stored 30-site baseline
comparison via `postrank_example()`:

```{r gallery-load}
library(postrank)
one <- postrank_example("tutorial_one")
two <- postrank_example("tutorial_two")
frontier <- postrank_example("tutorial_frontier")
commonality <- postrank_example("tutorial_commonality")
comparison <- postrank_example("comparison_30x3_tau35")
```

## 1. Report card (`postrank_plot_report_card()`) {#where-are-the-uncertain-scores-and-chosen-grades}

`postrank_plot_report_card()` plots each entity's posterior mean and equal-tail
marginal interval colored by its assigned integer grade (`autoplot()` on a
`postrank_analysis` or `postrank_report_card` calls this plot by default):

```{r gallery-card, fig.cap="Posterior means, 90% equal-tail marginal intervals, and assigned grades on Score A across the six tutorial sites (Grade 1 has highest priority).", fig.alt="Horizontal interval plot of Score A posterior means and 90% intervals for sites A through F, colored by Grades 1, 2, and 3."}
postrank_plot_report_card(one)
```

Each horizontal bar summarizes marginal uncertainty about one entity's target
score rather than an uncertainty interval for its grade assignment. With
multiple criteria, separate panels keep each criterion on its own units (`ncol`
sets the panel layout). By default, `max_rows = 30L` spreads a bounded display
sample across occupied grades and notes the selection in the subtitle; pass
`entities` to select specific IDs or display more rows, `entity_labels` and
`criterion_labels` to rename axes without altering stored IDs, and `order_by`
whenever `order = "mean"` is used with more than one displayed criterion.

## 2. Pair relations (`postrank_plot_relations()`) {#which-comparisons-did-the-report-disclose}

`postrank_plot_relations()` plots the pairwise ordering decisions of one grading
(`autoplot()` on a `postrank_fit` or `postrank_baseline` calls this plot by
default; when a second grading `y` is supplied, it plots the pairwise ordering
changes from `x` to `y`):

```{r gallery-relations, fig.cap="Pairwise ordering decisions of the two-criterion common grading across sites A through F: A through D share Grade 1 (left unordered), ahead of E (Grade 2) and F (Grade 3).", fig.alt="Six-by-six relation matrix showing sites A through D unordered relative to one another in Grade 1 and ordered ahead of E and F."}
postrank_plot_relations(two)
```

Cells display the grading decision (`1` row ahead of column, `-1` column ahead
of row, `0` shared grade) rather than posterior comparison probabilities—an
unordered cell does not imply a `0.5` comparison probability. Only the relative
order of integer grade labels matters (`canonical_postrank_grade()` preserves
every cell). Use `labels = "none"` to hide tick labels on large entity sets; if
a fit has no checked grading, the plot displays its solver status instead.

## 3. Criterion error profile (`postrank_plot_profile()`) {#how-does-each-criterion-contribute}

`postrank_plot_profile()` plots per-criterion expected wrong-direction errors
per ordered pair (`show = "E_over_N"`, the default), per all unordered pairs
(`show = "E_over_M"`), or criterion loss (`show = "risk"`, which includes `tau`
on unordered pairs):

```{r gallery-profile, fig.cap="Expected wrong-direction errors per ordered pair (E/N) on Score A and Score B under the equal-weight two-criterion grading, with point size proportional to criterion weight.", fig.alt="Horizontal dot plot of expected wrong-direction errors per ordered pair on Score A (0.0177) and Score B (0.0267)."}
postrank_plot_profile(two)
```

Equal weights in the loss objective do not force equal error rates across
criteria. When a grading leaves all pairs unordered (`N = 0`), `E_over_N` is
`NA` (omitted with a note) while `E_over_M` is `0`. When `show = "E_over_N"`
and `budgets = TRUE`, vertical tick marks indicate any declared per-criterion
error budgets `q` (`show = "risk"` instead draws a dashed vertical line at
`tau`), and zero-weight criteria with finite values appear as small hollow
circles.

## 4. Pairwise error probabilities (`postrank_plot_pairwise()`) {#what-probabilities-were-supplied-to-the-decision}

`postrank_plot_pairwise()` displays the input directional-error probabilities
`e[i, j, k]`—the posterior probability $\Pr(\theta_{ik} \le \theta_{jk})$ that
placing row entity `i` ahead of column entity `j` on criterion `k` is wrong:

```{r gallery-pairwise, fig.cap="Input directional-error probabilities Pr(theta_i <= theta_j) on Score A and Score B across the six tutorial sites; gray diagonal cells mark self-comparisons (NA).", fig.alt="Two side-by-side six-by-six heatmaps of directional-error probabilities for Score A and Score B, with gray diagonal cells."}
postrank_plot_pairwise(two, ncol = 2L)
```

Self-comparisons on the diagonal are `NA` (drawn in gray) rather than zero-error
pairs. By default, `max_entities = 20L` bounds the matrix size (`max_entities = NULL`
draws all entities). `postrank_plot_pairwise()` accepts `postrank_analysis`,
`postrank_fit`, `postrank_pairwise` (including `postrank_probabilities`), or
`postrank_coefficients` objects; call `postrank_pairwise()` first when starting
from raw `postrank_draws` (tie-aware `postrank_tie_*` objects have separate
three-way probabilities and are not plotted here).

## 5. Method comparison (`postrank_plot_compare()`) {#how-do-grading-rules-compare-under-the-same-loss}

`postrank_plot_compare()` compares a reference grading and alternative rules
evaluated on the exact same posterior and loss (`autoplot()` on a
`postrank_comparison`). Here `comparison_30x3_tau35` evaluates the four-grade
common grading alongside expected-rank and composite fixed-order cut baselines
across 30 synthetic sites on `poverty`, `frl`, and `snap` (`weights = c(0.5, 0.25, 0.25)`,
`tau = 0.35`, `G_max = 4`):

```{r gallery-comparison, fig.height=7, fig.cap="Loss, disclosure rate, and occupied grade count for the joint common grading and two fixed-order cut baselines evaluated under the same 30-site posterior and loss (ncol = 1).", fig.alt="Three stacked horizontal comparison panels showing matching loss, disclosure rate, and grade counts across joint, expected_rank, and composite rules."}
postrank_plot_compare(comparison, ncol = 1L)
```

Axis labels summarize each rule's solver status, optimality scope (whole allowed
family vs. contiguous cuts of one fixed score order), and optimization gap, and
flag any candidate that falls outside `G_max`, `exact_G`, or `q`. Setting
`view = "relations"` plots stacked counts of newly ordered, newly unordered, and
reversed pairs relative to the reference grading.

## 6. Withholding-cost frontier (`postrank_plot_frontier()`) {#what-changes-when-withholding-costs-more}

`postrank_plot_frontier()` plots the fraction of ordered pairs (`"disclosure"`),
per-criterion expected errors per ordered pair (`"error"`), and overall loss
(`"risk"`) across a grid of `tau` or `q` settings (`autoplot()` on a
`postrank_frontier`):

```{r gallery-frontier, fig.cap="Disclosure rate, criterion expected errors per ordered pair, and overall loss across tau = 0.05, 0.10, 0.20, 0.30, and 0.40 on the six-site two-criterion tutorial posterior.", fig.alt="Three-panel line plot across five tau values showing disclosure rising from 0.533 to 0.800, criterion E/N curves, and overall loss."}
postrank_plot_frontier(frontier)
```

Under exact optimization over a fixed allowed family, the number of ordered
pairs never falls as `tau` increases, whereas numerical runs should be read
alongside their solver statuses and gaps (`mark_uncertified = TRUE` draws points
whose solver status is not `"optimal"` as hollow circles; `"optimal"` records
numerical solver termination within tolerances and is not an exact mathematical
certificate). Missing or unvalidated grid points appear as breaks along the
path, and losses at different `tau` values come from different loss functions.

## 7. Commonality cost (`postrank_plot_commonality()`) {#what-does-each-criterion-give-up-for-a-common-grade}

`postrank_plot_commonality()` plots how much extra posterior expected loss each
criterion incurs under a shared common grading compared with a separate grading
optimized for that criterion alone at the same `tau` and `G_max` (`autoplot()`
on a `postrank_commonality_cost`):

```{r gallery-commonality, fig.cap="Extra criterion loss under the shared two-criterion grading relative to each criterion's own optimized grading on the six tutorial sites, with solver bound intervals [cost_lower, cost_upper].", fig.alt="Horizontal interval plot showing extra criterion loss of 0.0490 on Score A and 0.0145 on Score B."}
postrank_plot_commonality(commonality)
```

Each horizontal segment `[cost_lower, cost_upper]` reflects numerical solver
bounds for that criterion's own optimization problem (`cost_lower` subtracts the
criterion's best checked loss; `cost_upper` subtracts its solver lower bound),
not posterior uncertainty about the target scores. When the common problem
includes error budgets `q`, report whether `protection` dropped or kept `q` in
the single-criterion solves.

## 8. Underlying plot data and saving figures {#inspect-and-export}

`postrank_plot_data()` returns the full data frame (or list of data frames)
behind any of the seven plot types without applying `max_rows`, `max_entities`,
or display label maps:

```{r gallery-plot-data}
postrank_plot_data(two, "profile")[, c("criterion", "weight", "E", "E_over_N", "risk")]
```

Save any returned `ggplot` object at explicit dimensions with `ggplot2::ggsave()`
(using optional `svglite` for SVG output). For sensitivity analyses and export
recipes, see
[Figures and sensitivity to reporting settings](a7-figures-sensitivity.html)
and [Reading and exporting grading results](a6-reading-exporting-results.html).
